title: Passing in 3s: Check, Shoulder, Turn
summary: Dynamic movement, then passing in threes where the middle player checks, looks over her shoulder and receives facing forward.
setup: 4 minutes of dynamic movement first (jog, high knees, butt kicks, side shuffles, carioca, short sprints). Then groups of three in a line, 10-12 yards apart, one ball per group.
how: The end player passes to the middle player, who checks toward the ball.
Before the ball arrives the middle player glances over her shoulder.
She receives on her back foot, opens up to face the far player and passes on.
The passer follows her pass and becomes the new middle player.
coaching: Look before it gets to you
Open your hips so you can see the field
First touch away from pressure and toward where you're going
This is the center mid's movement in the build-out
easier: The middle player can take two touches and doesn't have to turn on the first touch.
harder: The coach calls 'man on' as the ball travels: the middle player must play it straight back instead of turning.

title: Build Out Through the Center Back and Center Mid
summary: The keeper, back three and center mid build out against three pressers and score through gates on the halfway line.
setup: Half field. Keeper plus left back, center back, right back and center mid against 3 pressers (2 forwards and a mid). Three small cone gates across the halfway line.
how: The keeper starts every ball.
The building team scores by passing or dribbling through a gate on the halfway line.
The pressing team scores by winning the ball and shooting on the big goal.
First 8 minutes: the center mid must touch the ball before it goes through a gate.
Then add a fourth presser who marks the center mid.
coaching: Center mid: show in the space ahead of the center back, never right next to her
Center mid: if a defender is between you and the ball, move into a passing lane
Center mid: check your shoulder and turn forward when you can; if not, play back or wide and show again
Center back: split wide of the keeper with the fullbacks spread out
Center back: no pressure? Dribble forward into midfield to pull a defender and free a teammate
Center back looks in order: center mid's feet, the wide back, a ball into space for a forward
Center back: when the ball goes wide, stay central and slightly behind; talk and direct
Lose it: center back gets goal-side and delays instead of diving in
easier: Start with 2 pressers, or let the building team use a 6th player (a wide mid).
harder: Add the 4th presser on the center mid from the start, or give the builders 10 seconds to reach a gate.

title: Balls Into Space: End Zone Game
summary: 4v4 plus 2 neutrals. A goal only counts when a teammate runs onto a pass into the end zone.
setup: 40 x 30 yard grid with a 5-yard end zone at each end. Two teams of 4, plus 2 neutral players who play for whoever has the ball.
how: Each team attacks one end zone.
A goal counts only when a teammate runs into the end zone and receives a pass there.
Passes to a player already standing in the end zone don't count.
After a goal, the scoring team keeps the ball and attacks the other end.
Progression: a goal scored within 3 passes counts double.
coaching: Pass to where she's going, not where she is
Runner: go before the pass, at an angle, and point to where you want it
Pass firm enough that the defender can't cut it out
Look for the run early; don't wait until it's covered
easier: Make the grid wider, or add a third neutral player.
harder: Two-touch limit, or the runner must finish with one touch into a mini goal at the back of the end zone.

title: Finishing Through Balls
space: Final third with a full goal
summary: A passer slides a through ball between two cones; the forward times a curved run, takes one touch toward goal and finishes.
setup: Keeper in a full goal. A line of passers at the top (center mids get extra turns) and a line of forwards near the sideline about 30 yards out. A cone gate about 22 yards out stands in for the defense.
how: The passer plays the ball through the cone gate.
The forward times a curved run so she stays onside and meets the ball moving forward.
One touch toward goal, then shoot.
Swap lines after each turn.
Last 6 minutes: a defender starts 3 yards behind the forward and chases.
coaching: Run so the ball comes to you moving forward; don't stop and wait
First touch out in front of you, toward goal
Shoot early, before the keeper sets
Low and across the keeper to the far post
Passer: weight it so the forward doesn't have to break stride
easier: No chasing defender, and the forward can take two touches.
harder: Start the chasing defender level with the forward, or add a recovering center back in front of the gate.

title: Scrimmage With Build-Out and Through-Ball Rules
summary: A full scrimmage against another team, with rules for the first 15 minutes that reward building out and through balls.
setup: Full field, 9v9 against the visiting team. Normal restarts except as below.
how: First 15 minutes: every goal kick is played short to the center back or a fullback, no long kicks.
First 15 minutes: a goal scored from a through ball counts double.
After that, play normally.
Coaches give quick sideline comments; don't stop play.
coaching: Center mid: show and turn when the keeper has it
Center back: dribble forward into midfield when no one presses you
Forwards: time your runs so you're onside and moving onto the ball
Shoot early once you're through
easier: Allow the keeper to roll the ball out to anyone on goal kicks.
harder: Keep the build-out rule for the whole scrimmage, or require 3 passes in your own half before crossing midfield.
